questions.q:
Assertion (A): A meter-bridge works on the principle of wheatstone bridge.
Reason (R): The drift velocity of electrons in a metallic wire is very high.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of the assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not correct explanation of the assertion.
If assertion is true, but reason is false.
Assertion is false, reason is true
questions.solution:
- Assertion (A): "A meter bridge works on the principle of Wheatstone bridge." True the meter bridge is simply a practical form of Wheatstone bridge used to compare resistances.
- Reason (R): "The drift velocity of electrons in a metallic wire is very high." False drift velocity in conductors is actually very small (typically of the order of mm/s), not high.
Hence \(A\) is true and \(R\) is false \(\rightarrow\) option (3).

questions.q:
Statement-I: A screw gauge having a smaller value of pitch has greater accuracy.
Statement-II: The least count of screw gauge is directly proportional to the number of divisions on circular scale.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct.
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are incorrect.
Statement-I is correct & Statement-II is incorrect.
Statement-I is incorrect & Statement-II is correct.
questions.solution:
- Statement-I: Smaller pitch \(\Rightarrow\) finer linear movement per rotation \(\Rightarrow\) higher accuracy. True.
- Statement-II: Least count LC = pitch / number of circular-scale divisions. So LC is inversely (not directly) proportional to the number of divisions. False.

questions.q:
There are four Vernier seales, whose specifications are given in column-1 and the least count is given in Column-II. Match the Columns-1 and II with correct specification and corresponding least count (\(\mathrm{s}=\) value of main scale division, \(\mathrm{n}=\) number of marks on Vernier). Assume (\(\mathrm{n}-1\)) main scale divisions are equal to n Vernier divisions.
\(\begin{array}{|l|l|l|l|}
\hline & \text{Column-I} & & \text{Column-II} \\
\hline \text{A.} & s=1 \mathrm{~mm}, \mathrm{n}=10 & \text{P.} & 0.05 \mathrm{~mm} \\
\hline \text{B.} & s=0.5 \mathrm{~mm}, \mathrm{n}=10 & \text{Q.} & 0.01 \mathrm{~mm} \\
\hline \text{C.} & s=0.5 \mathrm{~mm}, \mathrm{n}=20 & \text{R.} & 0.1 \mathrm{~mm} \\
\hline \text{D.} & s=1 \mathrm{~mm}, \mathrm{n}=100 & \text{S.} & 0.025 \mathrm{~mm} \\
\hline
\end{array}\)
questions.solution:
Least count (LC) of a Vernier \(=s / n\), where \(s=\) main scale division (MSD) value, \(\mathrm{n}=\) number of Vernier divisions.
- \(A: s=1 \mathrm{~mm}, n=10 \Rightarrow L C=1 / 10=0.1 \mathrm{~mm} \Rightarrow\) R
- B: \(\mathrm{s}=0.5 \mathrm{~mm}, \mathrm{n}=10 \Rightarrow \mathrm{LC}=0.5 / 10=0.05 \mathrm{mm} \Rightarrow \mathrm{P}\)
- \(\mathrm{C}: \mathrm{s}=0.5 \mathrm{~mm}, \mathrm{n}=20 \Rightarrow \mathrm{LC}=0.5 / 20= 0.025 \mathrm{~mm} \Rightarrow \mathrm{~S}\)
- \(\mathrm{D}: \mathrm{s}=1 \mathrm{~mm}, \mathrm{n}=100 \Rightarrow \mathrm{LC}=1 / 100=0.01 \mathrm{mm} \Rightarrow \mathrm{Q}\)
Hence option (2).

questions.q:
Match the columns.
\(\begin{array}{|l|l|l|l|}
\hline & \text{Column-I} & & \text{Column-II} \\
\hline \text{A.} & \text{Backlash error} & \text{P.} & \text{Always subtracted} \\
\hline \text{B.} & \text{Zero error} & \text{Q.} & \text{Least count } =1 \text{ MSD 1 VSD} \\
\hline \text{C.} & \text{Vernier callipers} & \text{R.} & \text{May be negative or positive} \\
\hline \text{D.} & \text{Error in screw gauge} & \text{S.} & \text{Due to loose fittings} \\
\hline
\end{array}\)
questions.solution:
- A. Backlash error \(\rightarrow\) (S)
Backlash happens due to loose fittings in the screw gauge.
- B. Zero error \(\rightarrow(\mathrm{P}, \mathrm{R})\)
Zero error is always subtracted (P), and it may be positive or negative (R).
- C. Vernier callipers \(\rightarrow\) (Q)
Their least count is given by \(1 \mathrm{MSD}-1 \mathrm{VSD}\).
- D. Error in screw gauge \(\rightarrow(\mathrm{R}, \mathrm{S})\)
Screw gauge can have zero error (positive or negative \(\rightarrow R\)) and backlash due to loose fittings (\(S\)).
